scope: At most two candidates; primary literature and public implementation review plus CPU-only counts from saved routing. No new quantized outputs or GPU execution.
candidate_a: Whether existing GPTQ-to-RTN fallback rules make materially different and correct choices under sparse expert calibration.
candidate_b: Whether collecting Hessians that an existing fallback will discard leaves meaningful avoidable calibration cost.

routing_check_frozen_before_execution.subset: Original train split only, 8 documents. Do not inspect validation outputs or quantization errors.
routing_check_frozen_before_execution.quantities: Per-expert routed token counts and per-document counts; apply 0.5% coverage and combined 0.5% plus 2*K rules analytically for gate/up K=2048 and down K=1024.
routing_check_frozen_before_execution.interpretation: Rule disagreement is not evidence that either rule harms quality. Rank deficiency alone does not prove GPTQ is worse than RTN.

stop_policy: End the review with one prioritized bounded diagnostic or no adopted research candidate. Do not launch a GPU experiment or expand to more candidates in this review.
